harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured the CentOS Stream 10 AppStream Redis-compatible Valkey service with durable AOF storage and a dedicated authenticated `inventory` identity. The generated credential remains undisclosed in `/etc/redis-inventory.env` with root-only permissions. A full node restart proved automatic service recovery and data persistence.
actions_performed: Installed and enabled Valkey 8.1.7, CentOS Stream 10's supported Redis-compatible package.
Enabled AOF persistence with one-second fsync under `/var/lib/valkey`.
Generated a 256-bit credential on node1 and stored it in `/etc/redis-inventory.env` as `0600 root:root`.
Created the `inventory` ACL identity using only the credential hash in the service ACL file; disabled unauthenticated default access.
Restarted node1 safely and verified its boot identity changed, the service recovered, and pre-restart data survived.

evidence.summary: Valkey is enabled and active; AOF with every-second fsync uses `/var/lib/valkey`. Startup logs show AOF replay, and the final persisted value is readable.

evidence.requirement: Dedicated inventory identity and root-only generated credential
evidence.summary: The generated 64-character hexadecimal credential is stored as `0600 root:root`; the ACL stores only its SHA-256 hash. Authenticated inventory access returns PONG while unauthenticated access returns NOAUTH.

Healthy baseline boot ID was `d4784d1b-162e-4faa-b581-f6427617d23c`; reboot was acknowledged; post-restart boot ID became `7da2e6e2-1ac7-49bf-9a9f-823b75422cde`. Service, listener, authentication, AOF recovery, credential permissions, and stored data all recovered.
